[ALUSI-FULL:v22p217#2/r12] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | Forgiveness may cover past sins or possible future lapses.
[ALUSI-FULL:v22p217#2/r13] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · قتادة | reports | Qatāda explains the noble reward as Paradise, with its incomparable delights and, above all, the vision of God.
[ALUSI-FULL:v22p217#2/r14] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · أبو حيان | reports | The conjunction orders the good news after following the reminder and fearing God; Abū Ḥayyān says the warning has benefited this person.
[ALUSI-FULL:v22p217#2/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · قتادة | reports | The reminder is the Qurʾān, and following it means reflecting on it and acting upon it.
[ALUSI-FULL:v22p217#2/r3] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | Alternatively, the reminder means admonition, and the past form of ‘followed’ denotes the certainty of future following.
[ALUSI-FULL:v22p217#2/r4] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | Alternatively, those warned are believers who already followed the reminder; warning alerts them to future lapses, avoiding a redundant warning.
[ALUSI-FULL:v22p217#2/r5] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | Alternatively, the phrase denotes those whom God knows will follow, the smaller group against whom the decree has not become binding.
[ALUSI-FULL:v22p217#2/r6] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | Fearing the Merciful means fearing His punishment rather than presuming upon His mercy; He is merciful yet inflicts painful punishment. | mentions 15:49, 15:50
[ALUSI-FULL:v22p217#2/r7] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | Calling God al-Raḥmān alongside fear signals the coexistence of great mercy with painful punishment.
[ALUSI-FULL:v22p217#2/r8] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | Al-ghayb may describe the absent punishment: the person fears it before it arrives and its terrors are witnessed.
[ALUSI-FULL:v22p217#2/r9] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | Alternatively, al-ghayb is a circumstantial phrase for the person fearing punishment while it remains unseen.
[ELMALILI:36:1-12#3/r14] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | Although most are unresponsive, the Prophet must warn everyone, since warning benefits and protects those who respond.
[ELMALILI:36:1-12#3/r15] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | Following the Reminder means seriously reflecting on and reciting the Qur'an and heeding its admonition.
[ELMALILI:36:1-12#3/r16] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | Fearing the Merciful unseen means revering His majesty while not yet in His presence, fearing punishment without presuming on His mercy, and obeying His commands; al-Hijr 15:49 holds mercy and painful punishment together. | mentions 15:49
[ELMALILI:36:1-12#3/r17] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | reports | Alternatively, “unseen” means inwardly, in the hidden heart that no one but God can know, rather than merely outwardly.
[ELMALILI:36:1-12#3/r18] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | People of any community who respond are promised forgiveness and a noble reward; the accusative nunation magnifies a forgiveness covering every sin and an honorable reward without favor or deficiency.
[ELMALILI:36:1-12#3/r19] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | The wisdom of the mission includes generous glad tidings as well as warning.
[TABATABAI:36:12/r1] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Effective warning reaches the person who follows the Qur’an, fears the Merciful with hope mingled into fear, and so may be given glad tidings of immense forgiveness and immeasurable reward.
[TABATABAI:36:9-11/r10] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | The restriction is an individualizing one: warning here means the effective warning that has an effect.
[TABATABAI:36:9-11/r11] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | The Reminder is the Quran; following it means affirming it and inclining toward it when its verses are recited, while the past tense signals certainty of occurrence.
[TABATABAI:36:9-11/r12] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | prefers | Fearing the Merciful unseen means fearing God behind the veil before death or resurrection unveils reality; the alternative of fearing him while absent from people is remote.
[TABATABAI:36:9-11/r13] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Calling God the Merciful suggests fear mixed with hope, which keeps a servant in worship without either complacency or despair.
[TABATABAI:36:9-11/r14] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | The indefinite forgiveness and noble reward magnify them: forgiveness is immense and the immeasurable reward is Paradise; the context supports the interpretation.
[ASAD-NOTES:36:11#n9/r1] ASAD-NOTES, d. 1412 · author | holds | The literal wording is ‘who is following the reminder.’

 holds | Verses 1–12 establish Muhammad’s prophethood: the wise Qur’an is the strongest evidence that he is God’s messenger calling people to the straight path.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p370/r5] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | The Qur’an is God’s favor to people who lacked divine guidance and wandered astray; arrogance makes them deny it, while inherited traditions and future desires block reflection.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p370/r6] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | The Prophet should not worry over those who will not listen; he should promise a great reward to those who fear God and are ready to receive counsel.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p370/r7] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | The Prophet should leave nonlisteners to God, who has recorded their deeds and can deal with them.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p376/r1] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | Reminders benefit those who heed counsel, open their hearts, and reason beyond the senses; valuable faith is professed through sight, hearing, mind, and heart before direct visual proof, while the Prophet leaves sight-demanders to God.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p376/r2] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | Fear of God follows from His graciousness: He must reward the pious and punish wrongdoers, so the appointed Day displays mercy and justice perfectly.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:11/r1] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · İbn Atıyye | reports | The word only limits who benefits from the warning, not who falls within its scope.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:11/r2] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · Müfessirler | reports | Most commentators understand dhikr here to mean the Qur’an.
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:36:11/r3] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · Râzî | reports | Others take dhikr to mean Qur’anic signs or clear proofs that complete human nature.
[SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p796/r1] SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT · author | holds | Warning is not restricted to unbelievers and hypocrites: believers are warned as a reminder to fulfill their duties, and the Qur’an also addresses the Prophet’s kin and those fearing resurrection.
[STUDYQURAN:36:10/r3] STUDYQURAN · author | holds | These verses remind the Prophet that he cannot guide those God has not guided and should leave them to God, as 35:8 states. | mentions 35:8
[STUDYQURAN:36:10/r4] STUDYQURAN · IK, Q, R, Ṭ | reports | The Reminder refers to the Quran itself, also discussed as Reminder at 36:69. | mentions 36:69
[STUDYQURAN:36:10/r5] STUDYQURAN · Q, Ṭs | reports | “Fears the Compassionate unseen” may mean worshipping God while God remains unseen. | mentions 50:33
[STUDYQURAN:36:10/r6] STUDYQURAN · Q, Ṭs | reports | Alternatively, the phrase may mean worshipping God in seclusion. | mentions 50:33
[STUDYQURAN:36:10/r7] STUDYQURAN · author | holds | The generous reward means Paradise or the Garden. | mentions 67:12
